newsitem.title: TAIWAN: Taiwan money rates rise amid tight liquidity.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan money rates rise amid tight liquidity.

text.p: Taiwan's money rates continued to rise at midday on Wednesday amid tightening liquidity in the banking system over the stock market's recent rallies, dealers said.
A bull run in the stock market -- where turnover eclipsed T$100 billion in the past few days -- is expected to continue attracting liquidity flows from the banking system, dealers said.
The overnight interbank rate was at 5.489 percent against Tuesday's 5.433 close, with the 30-day commercial paper at 5.50 percent against 5.20-5.50.
Traders saw some buying interest in the government bond market in the morning despite the bullish stock market, which has attracted most investment interest in the past few days.
The 10-year 84/1 yield was at 5.8400 percent, the seven-year 85/3 yield was at 5.7350, the seven-year 86/3 was at 5.8300 and the 10-year 86/4 was at 5.9950-6.0000.
